situation: In September, Garoua receives short, very heavy afternoon storms with thunder. Emmanuel's cousin in Buea, on the slope of Mount Cameroon, says that it rains there for many days, with low clouds against the mountain.
Emmanuel wonders why the rain is so different in the two towns.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Emmanuel does not understand why the rain in Garoua is different from the rain in Buea.
Describe the rain in Garoua and in Buea.
In Garoua, the rain falls in short, heavy afternoon storms with thunder. In Buea, it falls for many days, with low clouds against the mountain.
How can Emmanuel compare the amount of rain in the two towns?
He can compare the rainfall measured with rain gauges at the weather stations of the two towns.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand how rain forms, how it is measured and why there are different types of rainfall.

qa.q: Rain, drizzle, hail and snow all fall from clouds. What is their general name?
When do the tiny droplets of a cloud fall as rain?
qa.a: They fall when they join together and become too heavy to stay in the air.

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: Precipitation is any form of water, liquid or solid, that falls from clouds to the Earth's surface.
items: The main forms are rain, drizzle (very fine drops), hail (balls of ice), snow (ice crystals) and sleet (rain mixed with snow).

qa.q: Look at the diagram. Name the instrument and explain how it is used.
qa.a: It is a rain gauge. The funnel collects rain into a jar. Every day, the water is poured into a measuring cylinder and read in millimetres.

qa.q: Why is the rim of the rain gauge placed about 30 cm above the ground, in an open space?
qa.a: This prevents rain splashing in from the ground, and keeps trees and buildings from blocking the rain.

sum.title: II. Measurement
items: Rainfall is measured with a rain gauge (pluviometer), in millimetres (mm). Its rim is about 30 cm above the ground, in an open space. Rainfall is shown with isohyets.

qa.q: What makes the air rise in each case?
In Garoua, the hot ground heats the air, which rises quickly and forms storm clouds. What type of rainfall is this?
qa.a: This is convectional rainfall. It gives heavy afternoon storms with thunder and lightning.

qa.q: In Buea, moist air from the Atlantic is forced to rise over Mount Cameroon. What type of rainfall is this, and what happens on the other side?
qa.a: This is relief (orographic) rainfall. The windward slope receives a lot of rain, while the leeward slope is dry: it is in a rain shadow.

qa.q: In Europe, warm air rises slowly over cold air. What type of rainfall is this?
qa.a: This is frontal (cyclonic) rainfall. It gives long, steady rain over a wide area.

sum.title: III. Types of Rainfall
sum.intro: Rain forms when moist air rises, cools to its dew point and condenses. There are three types of rainfall, according to the cause of rising:
items: The sun heats the ground and the air above it, which rises quickly and forms cumulonimbus clouds. It gives heavy afternoon storms, as in Garoua.
Moist air is forced to rise over a mountain. The windward slope is wet and the leeward slope is dry (rain shadow), as around Mount Cameroon.
Warm, light air rises over cold, heavy air along a front. It gives long, steady rain, mainly in temperate regions.

evaluation: Three forms of precipitation are rain, hail and drizzle.
Why is the leeward slope of a mountain dry?
The air has lost its moisture on the windward slope, and it warms as it goes down, so it gives little rain.
What type of rainfall is most common in Garoua? Explain.
Convectional rainfall is most common, because the hot ground heats the air, which rises quickly and forms storm clouds.
remediation: Any water falling from clouds is called ______.
Rainfall is measured with a ______, in mm.
A line joining places of equal rainfall is an ______.
Rain caused by hot ground heating the air is ______ rainfall.
Rain caused by air rising over a mountain is ______ rainfall.
The dry side of a mountain is in a rain ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. precipitation 2. rain gauge 3. isohyet 4. convectional 5. relief (orographic) 6. shadow
end.homework: Observe the wind in Garoua for three days: from which direction does it blow? Is it dry or moist? Write your observations.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 36: Pressure Belts and Planetary Winds.
teacherNote: Debundscha, at the foot of Mount Cameroon, receives about 10,000 mm of rain per year, one of the highest totals in the world: a clear example of relief rainfall.
Frontal rainfall is rare in Cameroon, but the meeting of air masses along the Inter-Tropical Front (ITF) controls the start of the rainy season.
